turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr. Iyer, keep the arm relaxed. First reading is one hundred and seventy-two over one hundred and four.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): One seventy-two? That cannot be my usual pressure, sister. I have come only for this right knee, nothing else, I am not a BP patient.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Appa, sit properly, you were almost running from the auto.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Actually what happened is, near the temple steps I missed one step, not a full fall, um, just a small twist, and from that evening there is this dull pain inside the right knee. It is there from five-ish weeks, not exactly to the day, around that only, and it catches when I climb.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): I will recheck after you sit quietly for two minutes. Any chest pain or giddiness just now?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no, nothing like that. No chest pain, no giddiness, no headache also. Sorry, I talk too much, that is my habit only.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Dr. Menon. Is it the knee you came for?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor, the right knee. This BP, whenever I enter a clinic it shoots up, pure white coat. At home I feel absolutely normal, I am telling you.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Swelling? Giving way? Locking?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No swelling that I have seen, it does not give way, and it does not lock. The ache is worse on stairs, better if I sit with the leg straight for some time.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any tablet for it?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I took one Crocin, five hundred milligram, by mouth, the night before last, for the pain, only that single dose, then I stopped. My stomach felt a bit heavy after it, but that settled by morning. I am not on any BP tablet, never have been.
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, his father had a stroke, that is why I pushed him to come. I did not want us to ignore a high reading.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Noted. Diabetes? Heart problem?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No diabetes, no heart problem. BP was never told high before, except these clinic readings, and even those I do not trust.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Smoke? Alcohol?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I never smoked. Alcohol, only at weddings, maybe twice a year, one small peg, that is all. I am retired from the accounts department at the mill, and I walk to the market most mornings.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Appa, do not start on yesterday's match, the doctor has other patients.

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, but it was such a match, doctor, India were fifty for three and I was so tense, then Kohli settled and they crossed two hundred easily. My neighbour was shouting from the balcony the whole evening, very disturbing, but nice also.
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the weather was so heavy we could not go to the terrace for the fireworks after the win. Coming back, the auto sat near the flyover for forty minutes.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Forty minutes, yes, and the driver was playing old Ilaiyaraaja songs, my grandson would have loved it, he is just learning the keyboard, poor boy practices till late.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. Back to the knee. Pain on flat walking?

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Flat walking is okay, doctor. Bending is possible, but the last bit on the stairs is where it catches. No fever, no redness, I checked in the mirror this morning, skin looks the same both sides.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me look.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): No swelling, no warmth. Bend and straighten are both full. Tender on the inner side of the right knee. That is all.
[SEG0026] person_1 (NURSE): Second reading, after sitting, one hundred and fifty-six over ninety-two.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): See, already coming down. If you check a third time it will be one-thirty only, I know my body. The cuff itself makes me nervous, my heart goes fast, then it settles. Classic white coat.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pulse is eighty-four, regular. I am not calling this established hypertension today.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): It may be white coat. It may be early hypertension. I cannot separate them on two readings.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So no tablet today?
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): No tablet today. No point starting a BP medicine on clinic numbers alone.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Get a home reading morning and evening, sitting, for seven days. Write every number and bring the paper.

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): We can use my wife's machine, she checks her own pressure, she takes telmisartan forty milligram at night, but that is hers, I have not touched those tablets. I will make a full table, date and time, I am very particular with records from my accounts days.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): One arm only, the right, same each time, after sitting five minutes.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Right arm, five minutes, morning and evening, seven days. And the knee, you are not sending me for any scan?
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): No scan now. If it is not better in three weeks, then an X-ray.

[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Avoid deep squats, take the stairs slowly. Paracetamol five hundred milligram by mouth, up to three times a day if the pain needs it, with food. Skip it on days you are comfortable.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Three times only if needed, with food, no squats. If the paper shows high BP, which tablet will you give, because my neighbour got a bad cough from one of them and I do not want that kind of trouble.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): We decide after the seven days. I am not naming a tablet now. Come back with the readings in one week.
[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will bring him. Should he worry about the stroke thing tonight?

[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not tonight. Pulse is steady and there is no chest pain. If he gets chest pain, a severe headache, or weakness on one side, go to emergency. Otherwise just the one-week visit.

[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Understood, doctor. One week, readings written properly, knee advice followed, and I will not borrow her telmisartan, promise. Sorry for the long match story, I get carried away.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): There is no BP medicine to print. Collect the slip for the knee advice at the desk on your way out.

spec.situation: Patient attends for something minor (a knee or a form) and the nurse finds high BP; BP read aloud twice with different numbers; patient says it is white coat; family history of stroke said in passing; no tablets started today, home monitoring arranged.
features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

bad.reason: Fast heart with cuff is reported, but resolution is not explicitly stated.
bad.text: Fast heartbeat (category=cardiovascular, status=resolved, temporality=resolved, aggravating_factors=blood pressure cuff, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Patient denied taking any blood pressure medication and said he has never been on a BP tablet.
Patient stated blood pressure had never previously been told high except at clinic readings, which he attributes to white coat effect.
Negative finding: no redness of the right knee skin and patient said the skin looked the same on both sides.
Examination finding: pulse was regular at 84 bpm.
Doctor stated he is not calling this established hypertension today and that there is no point starting a BP medicine on clinic numbers alone; no BP tablet today.
Home blood pressure monitoring instruction included using the same arm each time, specifically the right arm.
